title: Earth Systems / Physical Geology
description: Builds a rigorous Earth-systems understanding of physical geology—Earth materials, tectonics, surface processes, water, hazards, geologic time, field interpretation, and human-Earth interactions—using real observations, maps, and data.

topics.title: Earth as an Integrated System
topics.description: This opening unit frames geology as a systems science linking the solid Earth, water, atmosphere, climate, life, and human activity.

children.title: Earth system spheres
children.description: Students learn the parts of the Earth system and how matter and energy move among them.

children.title: Feedbacks and cycles
children.description: Systems thinking helps students explain why local geologic processes can have global consequences.

children.title: rock cycle and water cycle coupling
Scientific evidence and uncertainty
children.description: Students learn how Earth scientists infer processes from incomplete records and noisy data.

topics.title: Minerals and Rock Classification
topics.description: Earth materials are the evidence base for geology. This unit teaches students to identify minerals and rocks and infer how they formed.

children.title: Mineral properties
children.description: Students learn diagnostic properties that reveal composition and crystal structure.

children.title: Igneous rocks
children.description: Igneous textures and compositions record cooling history and magma chemistry.

children.title: Sedimentary and metamorphic rocks
children.description: These rocks preserve surface processes, environments, burial, deformation, and heating.

topics.title: Plate Tectonics and Earth Interior
topics.description: Plate tectonics is the unifying theory of physical geology, explaining earthquakes, volcanoes, mountains, oceans, and long-term Earth evolution.

children.title: Earth's internal structure
children.description: Students learn how the planet's layered structure drives surface behavior.

children.title: Plate boundaries
children.description: Boundary types organize many geologic hazards and landforms.

children.title: Driving mechanisms and evidence
children.description: Students connect the theory to observations rather than memorizing boundary names.

topics.title: Geologic Time and Earth History
topics.description: Geology requires thinking across immense timescales. This unit teaches how Earth scientists date events and reconstruct past environments.

children.title: Relative dating
children.description: Students learn how sequences of events can be inferred without exact ages.

children.title: Radiometric dating
children.description: Absolute dating turns isotope systems into numerical ages.

children.title: Earth history and stratigraphy
children.description: Rocks become historical records of environments, life, climate, and tectonics.

topics.title: Weathering, Soils, and Critical Zone Processes
topics.description: The critical zone is where rock, water, air, organisms, and human activity interact to produce soil and regulate resources.

children.title: Physical and chemical weathering
children.description: Students learn how rocks break down mechanically and chemically at Earth's surface.

children.title: Soil formation
children.description: Soils record climate, organisms, parent material, topography, and time.

children.title: Critical zone services
children.description: Students connect weathering and soils to water quality, agriculture, carbon storage, and hazards.

topics.title: Surface Processes and Landforms
topics.description: Landscapes evolve through water, ice, wind, gravity, tectonics, and climate. This unit teaches students to read landforms as process records.

children.title: Fluvial systems
children.description: Rivers shape landscapes and transfer water, sediment, and pollutants.

children.title: Glacial and arid landscapes
children.description: Contrasting process environments show how climate controls landform development.

children.title: Mass wasting and hillslopes
children.description: Slope processes link weathering, gravity, water, and hazards.

topics.title: Groundwater, Aquifers, and Watersheds
topics.description: Groundwater and surface water connect geology to ecosystems, drinking water, contamination, drought, and land-use decisions.

children.title: Groundwater flow
children.description: Students learn how water moves through porous and fractured Earth materials.

children.title: Aquifers and wells
children.description: Aquifer behavior explains water supply, depletion, and contamination risk.

children.title: Watershed water budgets
children.description: Students connect precipitation, runoff, evapotranspiration, and storage.

topics.title: Volcanoes, Magma, and Igneous Systems
topics.description: Volcanism reveals Earth's internal heat and creates hazards, resources, landforms, and atmospheric impacts.

children.title: Magma generation and composition
children.description: Students learn why magma forms and how composition controls eruption behavior.

children.title: Volcanic landforms and deposits
children.description: Volcanic deposits preserve eruption style and hazard history.

children.title: Volcanic hazards and monitoring
children.description: Students connect geologic evidence to risk reduction.

topics.title: Earthquakes, Faults, and Seismology
topics.description: Earthquakes provide evidence for plate motion and Earth's interior while posing major societal hazards.

children.title: Fault mechanics
children.description: Students learn how stress builds, rocks fail, and seismic energy is released.

children.title: Seismic waves and Earth structure
children.description: Seismic waves reveal both earthquake location and internal Earth layers.

children.title: Earthquake hazard and risk
children.description: Students distinguish physical hazard from social vulnerability and preparedness.

topics.title: Coastal, Marine, and Sedimentary Systems
topics.description: Coasts and marine basins are dynamic interfaces among land, ocean, atmosphere, sediment, ecosystems, and people.

children.title: Coastal processes
children.description: Students learn how waves, tides, storms, and sea-level change shape coastlines.

children.title: Marine sedimentation
children.description: Marine sediments record climate, tectonics, biology, and ocean circulation.

children.title: Sea-level and coastal risk
children.description: Students connect physical geology to climate adaptation and land-use decisions.

topics.title: Climate, Biogeochemical Cycles, and Earth Records
topics.description: A world-class Earth systems course should connect rocks, sediments, ice, and oceans to climate history and future change.

children.title: Carbon and nutrient cycles
children.description: Students learn how geologic and biological processes regulate atmospheric composition.

children.title: Paleoclimate archives
children.description: Earth materials preserve past climate signals.

children.title: Earth-system change
children.description: Students connect geologic timescales with modern climate and environmental change.

topics.title: Geologic Hazards and Risk
topics.description: This unit integrates earthquakes, volcanoes, landslides, floods, erosion, subsidence, and coastal hazards into risk analysis.

children.title: Hazard identification
children.description: Students learn to recognize where hazardous processes are likely.

children.title: Exposure and vulnerability
children.description: Risk depends on people, infrastructure, and preparedness, not only physical processes.

children.title: Mitigation and resilience
children.description: Students learn how science informs planning and emergency management.

topics.title: Field Mapping and Geologic Interpretation
topics.description: Field and map skills make geology concrete: students learn to observe, sketch, measure, map, and infer geologic histories.

children.title: Field observation
children.description: Students practice making careful observations before jumping to interpretation.

children.title: Maps, cross sections, and stratigraphic columns
children.description: Spatial representations help students reconstruct subsurface structure and time relationships.

children.title: Interpretive reasoning
children.description: Students learn to build a coherent geologic story from incomplete evidence.

topics.title: Geospatial Data, Remote Sensing, and Earth Observation
topics.description: Modern geology increasingly uses GIS, remote sensing, and open data to map landforms, hazards, resources, and environmental change.

children.title: Spatial data foundations
children.description: Students learn how location, scale, and projection affect Earth science analysis.

children.title: Remote sensing
children.description: Satellite and aerial data expand field observation across large areas and time.

children.title: Data workflows
children.description: Students practice reproducible, ethical use of Earth data.

topics.title: Human-Earth Interactions and Environmental Applications
topics.description: The final unit connects physical geology to resources, contamination, land-use planning, environmental justice, and sustainability.

children.title: Earth resources
children.description: Students learn how geologic processes concentrate useful materials and shape extraction impacts.

children.title: Pollution and environmental geology
children.description: Geology controls contaminant movement through soils, water, and sediments.

children.title: Decision-making and stewardship
children.description: Students connect geoscience evidence to public decisions.
